clue.text: A pie-man might be without the right fruit

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters go around the next piece
what a pie-man might be suggests these letters rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A pie-seller is pictured lacking the proper fruit for his wares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges A PIEMAN into PEAMAIN, and 'without' (meaning outside) wraps it around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearmain is an old variety of apple, so it is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Left among underwear sets

indicators.note: one letter placed among the letters of the garment word means it goes inside

parts.note: pants are underwear, in British use underpants or knickers

explanation.surface: Something left lying in a pile of underwear sets.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English pants means underpants, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants as a verb means puts in place or sets down firmly, as in planting a seed.

clue.text: On the water it could be fatal going around duck

indicators.note: the rearranged letters circle the next piece, which sits inside them
the word fatal could be something else, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so it gives O

explanation.surface: A warning that being on the water could prove deadly when circling a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' turns FATAL into AFLAT, and 'going around' puts O (duck, a cricketing zero) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afloat is floating, borne up on a lake or sea rather than sinking.

clue.text: Low soldiers poet

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle, which is moo
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Downcast troops are described as having a poet among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective meaning sad, but it is the verb for a cow's call. Thomas Moore was an Irish poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Moore was an Irish writer of verse, famous for Irish Melodies.

clue.text: Despicable lord following a serving man back

indicators.note: following places the lord's word after the reversed soldier in the answer
back tells us to read the soldier's letters in the opposite direction

parts.note: a GI is an American serving soldier
a lord is a noble, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A lord who trails after a servant is called contemptible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a serving man' reads like a butler, but it is an American soldier; 'back' reverses him and 'following' places the lord after.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means shameful or base, the opposite of honourable, so it matches contemptible behaviour.

clue.text: The attitude taken by a virtuous individual standing by an engineer

parts.note: a saint is a virtuous person, abbreviated ST
taken as written
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: A good person stands beside an engineer and adopts a stance on something.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the usual abbreviation for saint; CE, civil engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or point of view held on an issue, just like an attitude.

clue.text: Those losing heart telephone about the tying up

indicators.note: the word loses its middle letters, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
to ring someone is to telephone them

explanation.surface: People who have lost heart phone about a tying-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' strips HOS from THOSE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethering means fastening an animal with a rope, so it is a form of securing or fastening.

clue.text: There could be nine to do-possibly twelve

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the phrase may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A clock-watcher has nine things to do, perhaps twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NINE TO DO; the numbers in the surface hide that twelve means midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontide is an old word for midday, which is twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Aim to consume Cheddar maybe, though satiated

indicators.note: one word eats the other, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
Cheddar Gorge in Somerset is an example of a gorge

explanation.surface: Aiming to eat a lot of Cheddar cheese even when already full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheddar' suggests cheese, but here it is Cheddar Gorge, a famous English limestone gorge in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: Engorged means swollen or crammed full, much as someone satiated has had more than enough.

clue.text: Nobody on the square is really versatile

definitions.text: Nobody on the square is really versatile

parts.words: Nobody on the square is really versatile
parts.note: if nobody is square then everyone is the opposite shape; that phrase also means good at everything

explanation.surface: No one who is conventional is truly versatile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like the slang for dull, but the joke is about shapes: if none are square, all are round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone all-round has many skills, as an all-rounder in cricket bats and bowls.

clue.text: High-powered firm

explanation.surface: A company described as forceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong means powerful or potent in one sense and solid or unyielding in the other.

clue.text: Little Elizabeth's wages

parts.note: Bet is a pet form of the name Elizabeth, a short version of it
the possessive ending supplies its letter as written

explanation.surface: The pay earned by a girl called Bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wages' looks like a noun meaning pay, but it is the verb: to wage is to stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To wage a bet is to stake money, so wages as a verb means gambles or stakes.

clue.text: Bleat about speed, so it may be found

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: to race is to speed

explanation.surface: Bleating about speeding, so the culprit may be traced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BLEAT together with RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: If something may be found, it can be tracked down or followed to its source.

clue.text: Some households waste a terrible lot, he scoffs

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run concealed within them

explanation.surface: A man mocks the amount of food wasted by some families.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffs' looks like mocking, but it is British slang for eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff in British slang is to wolf food down, so one who scoffs consumes meals.

clue.text: A few words added, note, in church

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a few words added at the end of a letter
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A postscript and a musical note are slipped in during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a domed or vaulted recess at the east end of a church building.

clue.text: The papers holding one quarter show bias

indicators.note: holding means the word for papers keeps the next pieces inside it

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively
north is one of the four quarters of the compass, abbreviated N

explanation.surface: Newspapers that cover one district display bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is part of the definition: proneness is a tendency or bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Proneness is an inclination or tendency, a leaning towards something.

clue.text: To make a point, twist the French do!

parts.note: S, south, is one of the points of the compass
to wind is to twist or coil
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone twisting the French rules to make a point at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a verb or a party, but it is the slang verb meaning cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating them, as a con artist does.

clue.text: Nourishment for persons on a strict diet?

definitions.text: Nourishment for persons on a strict diet?

parts.words: Nourishment for persons on a strict diet?
parts.note: people on a strict diet may go without eating entirely, so their meal would be abstinence itself

explanation.definitionFit: Fast food is quick takeaway fare; the clue plays on fast as abstaining from eating.

clue.text: Agreement to effect a reduction

explanation.surface: A deal that will cut costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding deal between parties; to contract is to shrink or become smaller.

clue.text: A medico, sour perhaps yet loving

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word sour may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor who seems sour may yet be affectionate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SOUR into ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means feeling romantic desire, full of affection for another.

clue.text: The grit of a writer!

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising an author's determination.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand was the pen name of a French novelist, Aurore Dupin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand is gritty granular material, and George Sand was a nineteenth-century French novelist.

clue.text: A painter for example turning in anger

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

indicators.note: turning means the letters for an example are read backwards

explanation.surface: An artist growing angry.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts; 'turning' gives GE from EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage is fury, a violent burst of temper.

clue.text: Orderly and nurse content to bear up

indicators.note: the word for nurse has the next piece as its contents, held inside it

parts.note: to rear a child is to nurse or bring it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lug is to carry or bear

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly and a nurse happy to keep their spirits up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' and 'nurse' paint a hospital, but orderly is an adjective and nurse means bring up; 'up' reverses the carrying word and 'content' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular means neat and systematic, arranged in an even pattern.

clue.text: Hurt that makes a mother mature

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
to age is to grow older or mature

explanation.surface: Injury that causes a mother to grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is harm or injury done to something.

clue.text: Article on perfume giving a lift

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: An item about perfume that raises the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or rise, so it is an upward movement.

clue.text: Bird-man bringing a charge

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A birdkeeper bringing an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like an accusation, but a tithe was a tenth of produce paid to the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a levy or tax, historically a tenth of income paid to the Church.

clue.text: Drinks finally helping people to sleep tight?

explanation.surface: A last round of drinks helps everyone sleep soundly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old-fashioned cloth cap worn in bed; 'tight' also hints at drunkenness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightcaps are last drinks before bed, and also soft caps once worn in bed.

clue.text: Drags youngsters around European capital

indicators.note: the word for youngsters goes around the next letter

parts.note: tots are small children

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, as a capital starts a word

explanation.surface: Someone pulling children round a European capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European capital' suggests a city, but it is just the first letter of European.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or haul, much as one drags a load.

clue.text: An ass over gear-changing

parts.note: on can mean over, as in a book on a subject

indicators.note: changing means the letters of gear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A donkey working through its gear changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' gives ON (as in a talk on, meaning over, a topic), and 'changing' rearranges GEAR into AGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of Asia.

clue.text: Competition is of no interest to certain folk

parts.note: flat means dull or lacking interest
a race is a group of people of common descent

explanation.surface: Some people find competing boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat race is a horse race run without jumps, so it is a contest.

clue.text: Hate to appear half-dead before an examination

indicators.note: before places the half word ahead of the exam in the answer
half of the word means only its first two letters are used here

parts.note: a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Dreading an exam so much one looks half-dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe, a strong dislike.

clue.text: A good chance to check out

explanation.surface: An opportunity worth investigating.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a likelihood of success; to prospect is to explore an area for gold or minerals.
